app.title: ANN Streamflow Prediction Dashboard
app.summary: A person opens a dashboard over the results of a batch of neural-network models trained on a daily discharge record. It first shows the record itself: totals, the series coloured by its training and testing split, how values are distributed, and monthly averages. Next the person narrows the models by activation function and optimizer and compares their test-set scores in a ranked table, bars, an activation-by-optimizer heatmap and an error-against-fit scatter. They can then open any one model to check its predicted series against the observed one over a chosen date range, and set its training loss curves beside other models' curves. The result is a choice of the best configuration, with the evidence for it. A SQL box lets them query the stored results directly.

task.text: Pick the best-performing neural-network configuration from a grid of trained models by comparing test-set skill scores, and check that model's predictions against observed discharge.

data.text: A daily discharge time series split by date into training and testing periods. For each trained model there is a row of configuration and skill scores, an epoch-by-epoch loss log, and a series of actual against predicted values with residuals.
data.item: one trained model configuration (an activation function paired with an optimizer) with its scores, loss log and predictions

stage.text: comparing trained forecasting models after a hyperparameter sweep, before choosing one and writing up

mechanism.text: Multipage dashboard. Filters on the comparison page narrow every chart and the ranked table to the chosen activation and optimizer combinations. Choosing a model on the predictions page loads its score cards and its observed, predicted and residual plots, and a date slider limits all of them to one period. A multiselect on the training page overlays the loss curves of the chosen models.

field.text: data-driven streamflow forecasting with neural networks in hydrology

workflow.name: compare a grid of trained models and pick the best one

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: The home page reads the results database. It shows four cards (data points, models trained, best R² and average R²), the discharge series coloured by training and testing split, a histogram for each split and a bar chart of monthly average discharge.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Two multiselects, for activation functions and for optimizers, narrow the set of models. The table and every comparison chart redraw from what is left.

The filtered models appear in a table ranked by R² test, with a banner naming the best one. Alongside are horizontal R² bars coloured by activation, an activation-by-optimizer heatmap of R² test, an RMSE-against-R² scatter sized by MAE, and training time per model.

A model is picked from a dropdown ranked by R². Cards show its R², RMSE, MAE and RME on the test set. A date-range slider limits the actual-against-predicted line chart, the scatter against a 1:1 line and the residuals over time.

Several models are chosen, and their training and validation loss curves are overlaid on a log scale, followed by normalized validation loss. A convergence table lists each model's best epoch and total epochs, and flags the ones that stopped early.

steps.step: lookup a value by querying the results
steps.here: A SQL text area, preloaded from a menu of example queries (best per optimizer, rank within activation, monthly error), runs against the results database and shows the returned rows.

distinctive: The models form a full factorial grid of activation function by optimizer, so the grid itself is drawn as a heatmap of the test score.
The split into training and testing is by date, not at random, and the discharge series is coloured by split so the held-out future period is visible.
The skill scores are hydrological ones (R² read as Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency, RMSE, MAE and RME in discharge units), each reported for both the training and the test set.
Early stopping is read from the loss logs: models that ran fewer than the full number of epochs are flagged in the convergence table.
A built-in SQL editor with example queries runs over the stored results, so new comparisons need no retraining.

parts.title: Data overview
parts.summary: Shows how big the record is, the best and average scores, and the discharge series with its training and testing periods, distribution and monthly cycle.

parts.title: Model comparison
parts.summary: Filters the trained models by activation and optimizer, then ranks and charts their test scores and training times so the best configuration stands out.

parts.title: Activation by optimizer heatmap
parts.summary: Pivots the test score into a grid of activation function by optimizer, with each cell coloured and labelled, so the factorial sweep can be read at once.

parts.title: Actual vs predicted
parts.summary: For one chosen model, shows its test-set scores and sets predicted discharge against observed over a chosen date range, as a series, a 1:1 scatter and residuals.

parts.title: Training analysis
parts.summary: Overlays the training and validation loss curves of the chosen models and tabulates when each converged or stopped early.

parts.title: Database explorer
parts.summary: Lets the person pick an example query or write their own SQL against the results database, and see the rows it returns.
